what: Texas Pacific Land owns about 882,000 acres of land in West Texas, over the Permian basin. It collects royalties on oil and gas produced beneath it, sells and treats water for drilling, and leases surface rights.
customers: Oil and gas producers drilling on its land, who pay royalties, buy water and lease surface access.
money: a share of production from wells under its land
sourcing and disposal of water used in drilling
pipeline easements, roads and surface use fees
moat: A landholding assembled from a nineteenth-century railway grant that cannot be bought anywhere else, sitting over the most productive oil basin in North America, with no drilling costs.
risks: Oil and gas prices and Permian drilling activity set revenue
It has no control over when operators drill
Only two analysts cover it in this data
The shares trade at a very high multiple of earnings
opportunities: Operating margin of 74% and net margin of 60%, because it has almost no costs
Return on invested capital of 32% with essentially no debt
Water handling and surface leasing grow even when royalty volumes are flat
watch: Royalty production volumes and water services revenue.
